title: Multiply by a Million: Scale Invariance in LLM Negotiators
description: People take more risk with small stakes and discount large amounts less; we test whether LLM negotiators, whose task is identical at every scale, also respond to scale. Across five models (Gemma 4 31B, Qwen3.8 27B, gpt-6-luna, claude-haiku-5.5, and gemini-3.5-flash-lite), each playing 3,200 self-play games (16,000 games total) on 40 randomly drawn price ranges at $100, $100K, and $100M with and without a public appraisal and an opening clamp, every model opens closer to its own limit at $100M without the appraisal, and closing deals follow the scripted openings' midpoint across all five models. Mechanistic patching and steering in Gemma 4 31B (E5, E6) localize where the appraisal overrides the scale signal at Layer 41 of 60 on the price-writing tokens. Includes the main paper, separated supplementary appendix (Appendices A-F), pre-registered Study 3 protocol and frozen SHA-256 inputs, E5/E6 pre-committed predictions, analysis code, and derived results.
